name: Poligon Education Fund
mission: Poligon Education Fund (Poligon) is a national, nonprofit organization that fosters meaningful and long term relationships between the Muslim community, allies, and members of Congress. Poligon promotes positive policy change by teaching Congressional advocacy skills to the American Muslim community and educating policymakers on issues important to them such as Islamophobia, civil rights, and social, racial, and economic justice.

rich_narrative.summary:
Poligon Education Fund is a US-based advocacy organization that provides civic training, town hall resources, and policy briefings to help constituents engage with the federal government [4][6][8]. Founded in 2017, the organization addresses key civil rights and public policy topics including legislative changes and travel bans [7][10]. Poligon maintains <cite id="2">zakat eligibility under the fisabilillah category</cite> for donors seeking faith-aligned civic advocacy [2][4].

However, potential donors must consider significant financial concerns. <cite id="3">No financial filings newer than FY2023 are available — donors should treat this 3-year-old financial picture with caution</cite> [3]. In FY2023, the organization reported <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $32,150</cite> alongside <cite id="3">expenses of $131,029</cite>, meaning spending was over four times its annual revenue [3]. Furthermore, <cite id="3">CEO compensation was $65,000</cite>, which represents <cite id="3">202.2% of total revenue</cite> [3]. The organization currently maintains only <cite id="3">0.5 months of working capital</cite> and <cite id="3">$5,638 in total assets</cite> [3]. On program performance, Poligon serves approximately <cite id="4">12,000 beneficiaries</cite> at a cost-effective rate of <cite id="4">$10.92 per beneficiary</cite> [4]. The overall Program Ratio score remains unrated due to missing expense breakdown details [3].
